scenario.name: Test: Phase 1C follow-ups combined (one target, one attacker)
scenario.author: Thomas Shaw
scenario.description: One-target exercise of all three Phase 1C tier-3 follow-ups, since the services sit on different ports and don't interfere. A Debian 12 target runs three vulnerabilities and a Kali/MSF attacker shares its private network. The target's secgen_tests each run over the Proxmox QEMU Guest Agent and should report: * vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoor (port 21) — tier-3 PASS via test_msf_exploit in session mode (cmd/unix/interact + sessions -c). * Random Parameterised Website (port 80) — tier-3 PASS via test_http_exploit (SQL injection auth bypass driven as an HTTP POST from the attacker; no Metasploit module, bespoke app). * DistCC daemon (port 3632) — tier-3 FAIL (negative control): distccd is installed and listening locally, but an iptables rule drops the attacker's traffic to 3632, so the Metasploit exploit cannot reach it. This proves the tier-3 check is a real exploit test, not a rubber stamp, and that the firewall rule is surgical (21 and 80 still exploitable). Both systems share a 10.92.0.0/24 private network (logical VLAN 1): IP_addresses[0] 10.92.0.10 is the target, [1] 10.92.0.20 is the attacker.
